findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: Observed that there is not a Certified Food Protection Manager present during the inspection. PICs were notified -- their previous certification recently expired. PICs plan to renew their CFPM. Ensure that the PICs are CFPMs who are always present when food preparation is happening.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. [C]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment:
Observed an accumulation of soil residues on the following:
(i) the interior of the soda machine nozzles. CORRECTED: PIC was informed and cleaned the nozzles during the inspection until they were clean to sight and touch.
(ii) inside the ice machine. PIC was informed and instructed to clean and maintain the machine regularly to prevent contamination.
Ensure food-contact surfaces are clean to sight and touch.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed that several sanitizer buckets did not have a measureable amount of sanitizer in them - 0ppm (Chlorine) for the sanitizer bucket in the bar and 0ppm (quaternary ammonium) for the sanitizer buckets in the dish area. CORRECTED: PICs were notified and remade the buckets so that they measured a safe and effective concentration of sanitizer: 100ppm (Cl) for the bar sanitizer bucket made from bleach and water (1 capful of bleach to 1 gallon of water); and 200pm (quat) for the dish room sanitizer buckets (filled from the dispenser over the mop sink). Ensure that sanitizers are used per manufacturer instructions so that there is a safe and effective concentration of sanitizer for food-contact surfaces: 50-200 ppm for Chlorine-based sanitizer and 200-400ppm for quaternary ammonium.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(D) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (D) If another solution of a chemical specified under (A) - (C) of this section is used, the PERMIT HOLDER shall demonstrate to the REGULATORY AUTHORITY that the solution achieves SANITIZATION and the use of the solution shall be APPROVED. [Pf]

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed a gap between the exterior door and door frame so that there was visible daylight along the bottom of the door. PIC was informed and will repair the door or attach a barrier to avoid entry of insects, rodents and other animals.
findings.citation_text: 6-202.16 Exterior Walls and Roofs, Protective Barrier. Perimeter walls and roofs of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall effectively protect the establishment from the weather and the entry of insects, rodents, and other animals. [C]

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.comment: Observed an opened can of tomato purée that is stored in a cooler in its original can without a cover. Opened cans of food are not storage containers (once opened, the can itself can be source of potential contamination, especially if the food item is acidic). CORRECTED: PIC was notified, and the product was removed from the cooler so that it could be repackaged in a cleanable container. Ensure that food is protected from potential contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-307.11 Miscellaneous Sources of Contamination. FOOD shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301 - 3-306. [C]

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
findings.comment: Observed the scoop in the chips in the server area stored with the handle touching the chips. CORRECTED: PIC was notified and the scoop was moved to sit on top of the chip container where the handle does not touch the food. Since the handle is touched by bare hands it must be stored above the top of food. Ensure that scoops for ready-to-eat foods are always stored to avoid contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.12(A) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) Except as specified under (B) of this section, in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container. [C]

findings.title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
findings.comment: Observed single-use containers stored on top of the prep cooler upright where the food-contact surfaces are exposed to debris from above. CORRECTED: Staff were informed and inverted the containers so that the food-contact surfaces were protected from contamination. Ensure that food-contact surfaces are protected by either inversion or cover from a closed shelf or packaging.
findings.citation_text: 4-904.11(A) Kitchenware and Tableware. (A) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of FOOD- and lip-contact surfaces is prevented. [C]

findings.title: Toilet facilities: properly constructed, supplied, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed no lids on the trash cans in the women's restroom. PIC was made aware and will ensure that the women’s stalls each have covered trash receptacles.
findings.citation_text: 5-501.17 Toilet Room Receptacle, Covered. A toilet room used by females shall be provided with a covered receptacle for sanitary napkins. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
(i) Observed a broken gasket in the hot box in the kitchen; PIC was informed and will repair the gasket. 
(ii) Observed the mop sink needs to be resealed to the wall as the original seal has crumbled; PIC was informed and will get the mop sink resealed.
Ensure that all physical facilities are in good repair.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.  [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed mops drying on the floor in the mens rooms where they cannot drain or air-dry. CORRECTED: PIC was notified and moved the mops to hang above the mop sink where they can air-dry. PIC and Inspector also discussed that wet mops can sit in the upper basket of a mop bucket so they can drain and air-dry without contaminating the surrounding area. Ensure that after use mops are placed so that they can air-dry without soiling walls, floors, equipment, or supplies.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. [C]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed employee washed their hands, then turned the faucet off with their newly cleaned hands. Reviewed proper handwashing procedure with PIC. Educate staff to use a barrier (such as a paper towel) to turn the faucet off after washing hands.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door. [C]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment:
(i) Observed an employee washing a cooking utensil in the cookline handwashing sink. CORRECTED: The practice was interrupted and employees were educated on proper use of handwashing sinks and proper warewashing procedures. Handwashing sinks should only be used for handwashing. Nothing else. When warewashing, utensils must be washed with soapy water, rinsed with clean water, submerged in sanitizer for the manufacturer-recommended contact time, and allowed to air dry before returning to use.
(ii) The bar handsink was observed to contain ice and a spoon. CORRECTED: Staff removed the spoon from the handsink and melted the ice. Ensure handwashing sinks are only used for handwashing, no other purpose.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. [Pf]

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: THIS IS A SECOND REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed containers of raw fish and beef stored over a container of tomatoes in the bottom of a prep cooler. CORRECTED: Staff moved around the food items so that the sliced fresh produce that is not getting cooked was stored above raw animal proteins that are getting cooked. Ensure that raw meats are always stored below ready-to-eat foods to avoid cross contamination, and that raw animal proteins are stored in order of final cooking temperature, with fish and eggs on top, pork and beef in the middle, and chicken and poultry on the bottom.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food. [P]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Multiple containers of whipped cream in the bar cooler were observed without date-marking. CORRECTED: Unlabeled whipped creams were labeled with the date they were opened. Any whipped cream containers that the PIC was unsure of the open date were voluntarily discarded. Ensure ready-to-eat, time/temperature controlled for safety foods are labeled with the date they were opened, and that they are used or discarded within 7 days of opening (day 1 is day of preparation or initial opening).
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1. [Pf]

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
Observed some of the staff working did not have Food Handler certificates. PIC is working on scheduling training for staff. Ensure that all staff who handle or prepare food and beverages have Food Handler certificates from an accredited provider by the next routine inspection.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically. [C]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment:
Observed employees missed several hand washing opportunities during the inspection:

(1) Employees did not wash hands before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with food.

(2) Employees touched gloved hands on their clothes and continued preparing foods.

The inspector educated the employees when the actions were observed. The PIC will also be continuing to educate employees about proper hand washing and glove use. Ensure that hands are always washed whenever contamination occurs.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Observed employees used their bare hands to turn off the faucets after hand washing. The employees were educated when the actions were observed. Ensure that a barrier is always used to turn off the facets to avoid re-contaminating clean hands.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
findings.comment: Observed the bar sugar scoop was stored with the handle within the sugar. The PIC was informed and the scoop was removed during the inspection. The inspector suggests storing the scoop outside of the container. Ensure that scoops for ready-to-eat foods are always stored properly to avoid bare hand contact with the food
findings.citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed a container of raw beef stored over a container of cilantro and onions in the right walk-in cooler. The PIC was informed and the cilantro and onions were moved onto the produce shelf during the inspection. The PIC educated the employees who stock the walk-in coolers. The inspector suggests hanging signs in the walk-in cooler reminding employees which shelves are for raw meat storage only. Ensure that raw meats are always stored below ready-to-eat foods to avoid cross contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment:
Observed the following food contact surfaces were not clean to sight and touch:

(1) The debris on the ice machine baffles - follow-up on 1/26/2026.

(2) The debris on the dry storage area seasoning scoops - the scoops were removed for cleaning during the inspection. 

(3) The debris on the bar sugar scoop - the scoop was removed for cleaning during the inspection 

Food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of debris. The inspector will follow-up on 1/26/2026 to ensure that the ice machine has been cleaned to sight and touch.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment:
Observed the following lacked proper date marking:

(1) The white rice that was not date marked in the left walk-in cooler - the rice was discarded during the inspection. 

(2) The chicken containers that had a label indicating it was prepared on 1/6 - the PIC knew that the chicken was prepared yesterday and the correct date mark of 1/15 was put onto the chicken containers.

Reminder that all temperature control for safety, ready-to-eat foods kept at the facility for longer than 24 hours must be properly date marked to indicate the seven day maximum (with the day the food was opened/prepared being day one). Ensure that required foods are always correctly date marked.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: Observed the back entrance door has a gap along the right side. Ensure that the gap is sealed (no light shining through) by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-202.15(A) Outer Openings, Protected. (A) Except as specified in (B), (C), and (E) and under (D) of this section, outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; (2) Closed, tight-fitting windows; and (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment:
Observed the following are not smooth, easily cleanable surfaces:

(1) The wood planks with peeling paint above the triple sink - re-paint the bare wood. 

(2) The caulking at the triple sink and back hand washing sink that is peeling away from the wall - remove the old caulk and re-seal the sinks to the wall.

Ensure repairs are made to make smooth, easily cleanable surfaces by the next routine inspection. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
Observed the following non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned:

(1) The dust on both kitchen walk-in cooler fans. 

(2) THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: The debris behind the soda nozzles at the bar soda machine.

Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris. Ensure that the above referenced are cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

The employees on the cookline were educated and the tomatoes were moved onto the top shelf during the inspection. Ensure that raw meats are always stored below ready-to-eat foods to avoid cross contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Observed opened bottles of chipotle ranch and buffalo sauce in the server area that stated they must be ‘refrigerated after opening’ stored at room temperature. The sauces were voluntarily discarded during the inspection. The PIC and employees that work in the server area were educated that any bottles that have ‘refrigerate after opening’ on the bottle must be stored inside of the cooler after being opened. The PIC mentioned they will likely switch to pre-portioning the sauces into small cups to store inside the server cooler. Ensure that temperature control for safety foods are always stored at 41F or below.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: Observed a juvenile, fast moving roach on the wall by the dish machine. There was not any other evidence of pests observed during the inspection. The PIC stated they have not seen any roaches recently. The facility gets routine servicing by Orkin every two weeks. The PIC was instructed to inform Orkin about the pest sighting at the next routine visit. The facility should prioritize cleaning and eliminating any pest entrance points. The inspector will follow-up in a month to check on pest maintenance.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (B) An iodine solution shall have a: (1) Minimum temperature of 20°C (68°F), (2) PH of 5.0 or less or a PH no higher than the level for which the manufacturer specifies the solution is effective, and (3) Concentration between 12.5 MG/L and 25 MG/L.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Observed a container of queso sitting on top of the containers inside the steam table with an internal temperature of 81F. The queso container has a label indicating that is was prepared at 7:30 AM. The inspector asked the PIC about the queso and they stated that it should have been put inside the steam table. The PIC voluntarily discarded the queso during the inspection. Ensure that temperature control for safety foods are always hot held at 135F or above.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.

findings.citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored.

findings.citation_text: 3-304.12(A) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.

Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris. findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use.
findings.comment: Observed several employee drinks stored on the cookline without lids and straws. Employees can keep drinks in food preparation areas if they have a lid and straw to prevent contaminating employee hands and exposed food. The facility has to-go cups with lids and straws that the inspector suggests employees using. Ensure that all employees have drinks with a lid and straw by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 2-401.11(B) Eating, Drinking, or Using TOBACCO PRODUCTS.(B) A FOOD EMPLOYEE may drink from a closed BEVERAGE container if the container is handled to prevent contamination of: (1) The EMPLOYEE'S hands; (2) The container; and (3) Exposed FOOD; clean EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, and LINENS; and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Observed an employee remove gloves and start putting on new gloves without hand washing in between. When the action was observed the inspector instructed the employee to wash hands before putting on the gloves. The PIC will be educating staff about proper glove use. Ensure that hands are always washed before donning gloves.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.

findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:

5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:

Ensure that food is always protected from cross contamination during storage. 

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed scoops (including, but not limited too, sugar and various spices) in the dry storage area soiled with debris. The scoops were removed from service during the inspection to be washed, rinsed, and sanitized. Ensure that food-contact surfaces and utensils are always clean to sight and touch. The inspector suggests increasing the cleaning schedule for the scoops. 

4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION: The inspector observed a juvenile roach by the taco shells above the steam table in the cook line room. The inspector discussed the pest issue with the PIC. It is recommended that the facility receive more frequent service from their pest control company. The facility should also ensure that all foods are covered and deep cleaning occurs on a regular basis (especially in hard to reach areas). All possible entry points should additionally be sealed (including holes in walls; see violation #55). Ensure that the premises is maintained free of roaches and other pests. 

6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Observed small holes in the wall near the taco shells above the steam table on the cook line and near the dish machine and dish drying racks. The holes need to be filled (i.e., caulked) to make smooth, easily cleanable surfaces. Sealing the holes will also eliminate possible harborage sites for pests. Ensure that all small holes are sealed by the next routine inspection. 

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Observed there is a missing ceiling tile in the cook line room above the large steam table. The PIC stated the old ceiling tile was recently broken. Ensure the ceiling tile is replaced to maintain physical facilities in good repair. 

6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Observed several sauce bottles that needed to be refrigerated after opening sitting on the counter (ranch and wing BBQ sauce). These bottles had been opened and sitting out for a significant amount of time as they were warm to the touch. The PIC stated he did not know these bottles needed to be refrigerated after opening. The bottles were discarded during the inspection. Ensure that all temperature control for safety foods are kept at 41F or below.

3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

findings.comment:
Observed the facility does not have signed employee health reporting forms. The PIC was provided with blank spanish copies during the inspection. The inspector will return on 09/19/2024 to check that all employees have signed the employee health reporting forms. 

2-201.11: (A) The PERMIT HOLDER shall require FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES to report to the PERSON IN CHARGE information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD. Report: Symptoms (all P except lesion), diagnosis (all P), and possible exposures (P).  (E) Responsibility of food employee to report symptoms/disease to PIC.

findings.comment:

The PIC was also instructed to educate staff about the proper hand washing procedure. Ensure that a barrier is always used to turn off the faucet after hand washing. THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION.

2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Observed an employee filling up a bucket with water in the prep line hand sink. The hand washing sink cannot be used for any purpose other than hand washing. The PIC was instructed to educate staff about proper use of the hand sink. Ensure that hand sinks are only used for hand washing. 

5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Observed the following food was stored in a way that caused the potential for cross contamination: (1) A plastic bag holding various items hanging touching taco shells; (2) Beef cooling on a cart directly next to the mop sink; (3) Container of salsa uncovered in the left walk-in cooler; and (4) Raw chicken stored over raw beef which were both stored over raw fish. All of the storage issues were corrected during the inspection. The bag was moved to a different location, the cart of beef was moved to a new location, the salsa was covered, and the raw meat was moved according to the proper storage order. Ensure that food is always protected from cross contamination during storage and holding.

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Observed scoops (including, but not limited too, sugar and various spices) in the dry storage area were soiled with debris. The scoops were removed from service during the inspection to be washed, rinsed, and sanitized. Ensure that food-contact surfaces and utensils are cleaned to sight and touch. The inspector suggests getting a regular cleaning schedule for the scoops. 

4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Observed beef and chicken sitting in containers beside the grill not being hot held. The PIC stated the food is cooked and then sits beside the grill until it is served (usually about 30 minutes). The inspector educated the PIC that the meat must be hot held. The chicken and beef were cooked recently and the ambient air temperature was 136F. There was still a large amount of meat left in the containers. The PIC moved around food to make room in the steam table. Ensure that foods are hot held to be maintained at 135F or above.

3-501.16: (A) (1) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 135F or above. Roasts can be maintained at 130F or above.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Observed a container of homemade salsa was not cold holding in a proper ice bath. The top of the salsa had an ambient air temperature of 52F. The ice did not cover every side of the container. The PIC moved the salsa into smaller buckets to allow the ice to reach every side. Ensure that TCS foods are maintained at 41F or less. 

3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment:
Observed there was beef and chicken cooling during the inspection in ice baths, but, there was one container of beef which was not in an ice bath. This container was siting on top of other beef containers. The beef had already been siting out for an hour and the internal temperature was still 140F. The PIC was educated and the beef was moved into an ice bath. After being put on the ice it had an ambient air temperature reading of 90F about 30 minutes later. Ensure that cooling methods follow an approved method. 

3-501.15: (A) Cooling shall be accomplished with time and temperature criteria by using following methods: FOOD in shallow pans, Separating FOOD into small portions, using rapid cooling EQUIPMENT, stirring food in container placed in ice bath, containers facilitating heat transfer, adding ice, other effective methods. P (B) When placed in cooling or cold holding EQUIPMENT, FOOD containers shall be: arranged to maximize heat transfer through container walls, loosely covered or uncovered, and during cooling period. C

findings.comment:

They get service from the pest control company every two months. The PIC should make the pest control company aware of the issue and get monthly pest control service for the next 6-months. The inspector will spot check the facility in 30 days to check on the pest issue.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment:
Observed several single-use articles stored with the food contact surface facing upwards. The PIC was educated and the single-use articles were flipped over during the inspection. Ensure that single-use articles are stored with the food contact surface facing downwards to avoid contamination. 

4-903.11: (A) clean EQUIPMENT and clean ARTICLES shall be stored in clean, dry location where they are not exposed to contamination and at least 6 inches above the floor. (C) SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be kept in original PACKAGE or stored in manner to protect it against contamination.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment:
2-102.11:  The person-in-charge (PIC) is not taking responsibility for properly educating staff on hand washing. PIC is also lacking in monitoring of cold holding. Today, discussed the facility’s need to create a daily log of the coolers within the facility. The preparation coolers are in constant contact with the hot temperatures of the kitchen. A daily log that is completed each morning allows staff to observe that coolers are properly functioning and holding foods at or below 41F. Educate your staff on proper hand washing and cold holding. 

Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by:  (A) Having no Priority Foundation items; (B) Being a CFM; OR (C) Responding correctly questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include C1 through C16.

findings.comment:

Discussed proper technique in the moment and halted the improper hand washing occurrence. Owner Luis is tasked with educating staff on the proper hand washing process. We have a hand washing educator and Spanish speaker that will be available in the next few weeks to provide education support. In the meantime, owner and CFPM should educate.  Follow-up to occur later than the normal three to ten days to allow for coordination of time with Spanish-speaker and educator. 
 FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED.

findings.comment:

Ensure that employees are using a barrier when turning off faucet handles after the handwashing process to prevent recontaminating freshly washed hands.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Observed an employee using the triple sink to rinse hands. Discussed with PIC that triple sinks are to be used for washing, rinsing, and sanitizing dishes only. Ensure that handwashing is done in hand washing sinks only and not triple sinks. 

2-301.15: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands in a HANDWASHING SINK only.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Observed chicken to be stored on top of steak and eggs inside of a prep cooler. Discussed with PIC the proper order of food storage. Ensure that foods are stored in a manner that prevents them for cross contamination.   

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.comment:

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment:
A prep cooler in the kitchen was observed to not be holding foods at proper temperatures. The temperatures of the food ranged from 51F-57F when probed. The food items consisted of but aren’t limited to pork, popcorn chicken, shredded lettuce, pico, diced tomatoes, etc. PIC mentioned that the items had been in the cooler since the morning. All food items were discarded and the unit will not be used until it can be serviced and functioning properly. Ensure that cold holding equipment is sufficient enough to provide proper cold holding temperatures for foods. 

4-301.11: EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
The facility is using quaternary ammonia as a sanitizer and there are no test strips. PIC mentioned that an order will be placed to get test strips. Ensure that test strips are available in order to properly test sanitizing concentrations. 

4-302.14: A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.
